pairs.why: The two drawings are almost the same; A's wagon has slightly softer, warmer shading, closer to the smooth rocking chair and boxing gloves, while B's ground is a little grittier.
They are close to identical, but A's canvas and wood are a touch smoother and rounder, like the real cards, and B reads slightly flatter and harder.
B's dirt ground has fine crack texture and its canvas is grainier, and the lessons mark texture as the tell; A is smoother.
B shows cracked-ground lines and a grainier canvas, while A keeps the soft, smooth finish of the real cards.
I can barely tell them apart; A's shading is very slightly softer, but this is close to a coin flip.
A's canvas cover has visible wrinkle and weave texture, and B's cover is cleaner and smoother, closer to the real cards' finish.
B's wheels and canvas look slightly smoother and more evenly lit, and A's cover carries a bit more surface texture.
A's canvas has a noticeable wrinkled-fabric texture, while B's is smoother, which the texture lessons say matches the real cards.
